newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM CEO sees scope for better '97 profit.
newsitem.headline: UPM CEO sees scope for better '97 profit.

text.p: Europe's biggest forest industry group UPM-Kymmene Oy's CEO Juha Niemela said on Tuesday that improving profits this year were possible but not certain.
"There are possibilities for better results, but we cannot rely on that development yet," Niemela told Reuters Financial Television in an interview to be broadcast later in the day.
"The price trend downward has stopped, but we can't be sure yet about the upturn," Niemela said.
UPM-Kymmene earlier reported a 43 percent fall in 1996 profit before extraordinary items to 3.56 billion markka.
UPM-Kymmene expected growth in Europe to be "slightly better" than last year, Niemela said.
"Also the destocking has now ended so we expect order books to be better this year anyhow," he said.
Paper prices would not start rising very soon.
"I don't expect a rally to take place, a gradual improvement is likely towards the end of the year," Niemela said, adding margins were "not really anymore" under pressure.
"Before we can really be sure of new price levels we must see demand picking up better than today," he told RFTV.
No dramatic cost cuts lay in store, Niemela said.
When asked about UPM-Kymmene's intention to reduce its 73.3 percent stake in engineering group Rauma Oy to below 50 percent, Niemela said:
"We have no schedule for it, but there is a firm decision to do it and that will take place some time in the future."
